newsitem.title: USA: Reich says any CPI revision should be technical.
newsitem.headline: Reich says any CPI revision should be technical.

text.p: Outgoing Labor Secretary Robert Reich said Sunday that any presidential call for revising how the Consumer Price Index is calculated should be a technical and not a political decision.

"It should not be a political judgment. It should be a technical judgment," Reich said on ABC's "This Week" program. "Let's leave it to the technicians, the researchers. The worse thing we can do, absolutely the worse thing, is to make this into a political football."

Changing the CPI, the country's key measure of inflation, became a major issue when a report by an independent panel earlier this month showed that the CPI overstates the cost of living by 1.1 percentage points per year.

Reich agreed that the CPI, which affects funding for a wide range of federal programs that are linked to inflation, should be revised and said The Bureau of Labor Statistics is "now working on that revision as we speak."

Earlier in the program, Senator Daniel Moynihan, a New York Democrat, said President Bill Clinton should either call for a revision of CPI in the budget or say he is open to discussion with the chairmen of the House and Senate budget committees.
Clinton is expected to unveil the fiscal 1998 budget on February 3.
